  "segment_function": "prologue",
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim": "The immediate reaction to the launch of the man-made satellite was relief about the first step toward escape from men's imprisonment to the earth, echoing the sentiment that mankind will not remain bound to the earth forever.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "The immediate reaction, expressed on the spur of the moment, was relief about the first “step toward escape from men’s imprisonment to the earth.” And this strange statement, far from being the accidental slip of some American reporter, unwittingly echoed the extraordinary line which, more than twenty years ago, had been carved on the funeral obelisk for one of Russia’s great scientists: “Mankind will not remain bound to the earth forever.”",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "confidence": 1.0
    },
    {
      "claim": "The earth is the quintessence of compound conditions and earthly nature may be unique in providing a habitat where humans move and breathe without effort or artifice.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "The earth is the very quintessence of the human condition, and earthly nature, for all we know, may be unique in the universe in providing human beings with a habitat in which they can move and breathe without effort and without artifice.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "confidence": 1.0
    }
  ],
